{{Quote|Many Bothans died to bring us this information.|Mon Mothma, before the Battle of Endor|<ref name="Episode 6">{{Film|VI}}</ref>}}
'''Bothans''' {{Pronounced|'bɑθən}} were furry [[Mammal/Legends|mammalian]] [[Humanoid/Legends|anthropoids]], about 1.5 meters tall. Hailing from [[Bothawui/Legends|Bothawui]] and several colonies, Bothans differed in facial appearance and body structure with [[Canine/Legends|canine]], [[Feline/Legends|feline]], and [[Equine/Legends|equine]] features. They were known for being master [[Politics/Legends|politicians]] and [[Spy/Legends|spies]], craving intrigue and subterfuge.

The Bothans were members of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] from at least [[4000 BBY/Legends|4000 BBY]], but likely from a significantly earlier point. Through numerous conflicts, most notably the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the Bothans remained officially neutral, although their famed [[Bothan Spynet/Legends|Spynet]] always played each side and commercial interests sought profits.

The Bothans were famously credited with [[Bothan Spynet intelligence operation/Legends|acquiring intelligence]] about the location of and [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] presence aboard the [[Death Star II/Legends|second Death Star]] during the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], enabling the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] to destroy the [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]]. However, many of them died to bring the Alliance this information. They played a large role in the founding of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] and in the development of its government.

[[Bothese]] was the name of the native language spoken by Bothans, where [[Botha]] was the written form.

==Biology and appearance==
[[File:Bothan_UM.jpg|thumb|left|180px|A Bothan.]]
Bothans were a short race of furry [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoids]] who on average stood between 1.5 meters<ref name="TEGAS">[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']]</ref> to 1.6 meters in height.<ref name="UAA" /> Bothans were covered in fur which shifted in response to their emotional state<ref name="UAA" /> by way of gentle ripplings. It was this trait, named [[Wrendui]],<ref name="Edge of the Empire Core Rulebook" /> that betrayed them when members of their kind intended to be duplicitous in their dealings with others.<ref name="TEGAS" /> They possessed tapered pointed ears, and both males and females were known to sport beards.<ref name="UAA" />

The Bothans were able to [[Hybrid/Legends|interbreed]] with at least one other species, as exemplified by the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] [[Valenthyne Farfalla]], a [[half-Bothan]].<ref name="EGTW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> [[Half-Bothan|Such hybrids]] somewhat resembled baseline humans with haunches, hooves, fur, pointed ears and a long tail.<ref name="JVS">''[[Star Wars: Jedi vs. Sith]]''</ref>

==Society and culture==
{{Quote|You have to understand that Bothans think in terms of political and persuasive influence, not military power. The typical Bothan's goal is to go through life getting more and more people to listen to what he has to say.|[[Sena Leikvold Midanyl]]|<ref name="Dark Force Rising">''[[Dark Force Rising]]''</ref>}}
Bothans evolved in forested mountains near the planet's equator, with no mounts or draft animals, unsuitable for farming or military conflict. This environment formed their culture: not only becoming artisans and craftsmen of wood and stone, but also controlling effectively any limited resources and avoiding direct conflict, preferring espionage intrigue instead. These traits made Bothans suspicious, opportunistic and scavengerous; control and influence was the supreme indicator of power, more than wealth.<ref name="guide" />

While Bothans did not possess real armed forces, warriors served as bodyguards for important persons, intended to prevent any internal conflicts.<ref name="guide" />

Bothan culture was guided by the philosophy and principles set forth in the ancient text known as [[Bothan Way|The Way]], written by [[Golm Fervse'dra]]. In this "Bothan Way", the pursuit of power and influence was paramount. Thus, individual Bothans put their own political and economic success above all other concerns, and as a species, Bothans put their own advancement ahead of other intergalactic interests, though many did side with the Rebel Alliance during the Galactic Civil war. The volume of backstabbing, subtle character assassination and political maneuvering in Bothan society was dizzying, and resulted in many species stereotyping Bothans as untrustworthy.<ref name="NEGAS" /> In fact, most Bothans are habitually paranoid, believing that anyone who's not working with them, is working against them.<ref name="NEGAS" />

In times of crisis, the focus of Bothan society shifted to a survivalist state known as "[[ar'krai]]." When engaged in ar'krai, all fit Bothans volunteered to defend their species from impending annihilation. The last calling of ar'krai was during the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] invasion after the death of [[Borsk Fey'lya]] and the practical defeat of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]].<ref name="NEGAS" />

===Clans===
<div style="float:right">[[File:Vital_Strike_SoC.jpg|thumb|left|200px|A Bothan conducting a Rebel strike team briefing.]]</div>
{{Quote|We don't all shmell alike! How do these rumorsh get started?|Kolir Hu'lya, a Bothan Jedi with a bleeding mouth during the Second Galactic Civil War|<ref name="Legacy of the Force: Betrayal">''[[Legacy of the Force: Betrayal]]''</ref>}}
Immediate Bothan families were organized into large clans, which were the most important social unit in Bothan society; family and clan loyalty were equally important as power accumulation.<ref name="NEGAS" /> The most ancient institution, clans represented a unity between families themselves, as well as their common heritage. Each clan had a presence in the [[Bothan Council]]. By the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] there were 608 clans with legal status, with 53 more new ones, emerging from small colonial settlements, petitioning. Alliances played a role for winning a vote in the Council for being accepted.<ref name="guide" />

Clan association was denoted as the last component in a Bothan name.<ref name="NEGAS" /> For example, the name [[Girov Dza'tey]] would mean that Girov was his given name, Dza his family name, and that he was of the Atey clan.

===Government===
{{Quote|I pity them, Councilor. I really do. For all the strength and mental agility they claim their political techniques provide to their species, I see them as an essentially unhappy people. Their whole outlook on life breeds mistrust, and without trust, there can be no genuine peace.|Elegos A'Kla|<ref name="Vision of the Future">''[[Vision of the Future]]''</ref>}}
The [[Combined Bothan Clans|Bothan Council]], a representative body of selective [[Clan|Bothan clans]], was the primary governmental body of the Bothan people. Renamed the "Combined Clans" during the [[New Republic era]], the body was still commonly referred to as the Council. At the height of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the council comprised representatives from 608 registered clans.<ref name="NEGAS" /> A constant flow of new clans petitioned for membership with the numbers soaring during crises like the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] invasion. At the head of the Council was the First Secretary, who led the council from their headquarters in [[Merchant's Square]] in the capital of [[Drev'starn]].

Beginning with the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] and continuing after the fall of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], the Council absorbed many of the Bothan political bodies, such as the [[Bothan Independent Treasury]], seeing them as wasteful, corrupt and inefficient. Highly centralized, the Bothan Council governed all social, political, economic and security issues of Bothan life.

The [[Bothan Diplomatic Corps]] was one of the few government organizations to survive the culling, and was in fact expanded. The Diplomatic Corp operated as a branch of the Bothan government, and held the responsibility of furthering Bothan ideals through diplomacy. Its agents met with the leaders of other worlds, forged treaties, and represented Bothawui in the New Republic, to ensure that Bothan ends were served in any alliance.

Although [[Bothan Space/Legends|Bothan Space]] have been prominent members of the New Republic and the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]] that replaced it, Bothawui joined the [[Confederation]] in [[40 ABY/Legends|40 ABY]] after the [[Assassin/Legends|assassination]] of several Bothan citizens on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] by the order of [[Darth Caedus|Jacen Solo]], and the revelation of a Galactic Alliance plot to invade Bothan Space.

[[Pers'lya]] was a Bothan [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] circa [[12,000 BBY/Legends|12,000 BBY]].

==History==
Their race evolved on the world of Bothawui which was located in the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]] and [[the Slice/Legends|the Slice]].<ref name="UAA" /><ref>''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> Their [[homeworld]] had an instable tilt; highest latitudes experienced regular [[ice age/Legends|ice ages]], consisting the northernmost and southernmost plains of the continents either frozen or barren. As such, [[forest/Legends|forests]] were concentrated near the planet's mountainous equator, where primitive Bothans settled and formed their civilization. Those who descended to the northern or southern plains became nomads, following the migrations of animals.<ref name="guide">''[[Shadows of the Empire Planets Guide]]''</ref> 

Villages were built in the forested valleys among the mountains; with no access to metals or farmlands, Bothans cleared the floors for farming, and used [[wood/Legends|wood]] and stone, mastering the crafts around these materials. The wealthiest families built higher on the foothills, with clan leaders building imposing fortresses on the mountains, controlling the passes, gathering taxes and protecting from invaders; in the Bothan view, elevation showed one's status and wealth.<ref name="guide" /> 

Whereas primitive species on other planets enjoyed the use of draft animals and mounts, the evolution of Bothawui's native fauna did not provide this commodity for the Bothans. It was Bothan porters who carried goods and merchantise on their backs, or pulled carts, over difficult terrains. As Bothans established their Great Halls and Clan Homes, the clans relied on controlling their limited resources among the forested mountains. Any conflicts that marked their early history proved to be disastrous for all sides; it was the porters, and the amount of supplies they could carry, that decided the duration of a conflict. In those cases, espionage proved to be more effective than direct assault. As a result, their culture veered away from armed conflict and leaned towards gathering information and probing for weaknesses of a rival, or waiting for a rival's mistake to act. As families meneuvered among clans moving after control and power, stratagems focused on intelligence and psychological warfare, aiming to weaken the unity of the opposing entity.<ref name="guide" />

Bothans were known to have developed the technology to travel through the stars millennia ago whereupon they became long standing members of the galactic community.<ref name="UAA" /> As materials like [[plassteel]] and [[duracrete/Legends|duracrete]] became available, they built more modern cities with [[starscraper]]s; but they kept their traditional aesthetic, making them blending with the older buildings, seeming like pseudo-stone monoliths, decorated with [[Fervse|glitterstones]].<ref name="guide" />

The Bothans were noted for being long time members of the Galactic Republic. In the millennia prior to the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]], the rapid expansion of [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperspace lanes]] led to a period of exploration. This saw the Bothans found their first colony of [[Kothlis/Legends|Kothlis]] along with a growing influence in the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]]. This era also saw the rapid growth of the [[Bothan Spynet/Legends|Bothan Spynet]] where their agents were sent to newly discovered worlds that saw Bothawui becoming a hub for information.<ref name="Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide">''[[Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide]]''</ref> 

[[File:GGW_Battle_of_Bothawui.jpg|thumb|left|330px|Bothawui, the Bothan homeworld, was witness to fierce battles between the Republic and the Sith Empire.]]
They were noted for being ever loyal allies to the Galactic Republic. However, Republic support was withdrawn from the long-standing allies as a result of the [[Treaty of Coruscant]].<ref name="Star Wars: The Old Republic">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''</ref> The Bothans were said to have mastered the art of intelligence gathering as far back as [[300 BBY/Legends|300 BBY]], and began exploiting it for personal gain. A [[200 BBY/Legends|hundred years later]], they made contact with the [[Dressellian/Legends|Dressellians]]; they recognized that species' potential and departed in order to allow them to evolve without interference.<ref name="TEGAS" />

Whilst a longtime member and supporter of the Republic, the Bothans remained neutral during the period known as the Clone Wars. In this time, the Bothan [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Polo Se'lab]] abstained from politically charged votes leading up to the conflict. Though not playing one side against the other, the Bothans served each one in a professional but not exclusive manner. Their reasoning for helping both the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatists]] and Republic was the belief that furnishing each side with intelligence would hasten the end of the war. This stance on neutrality did not stop both the Confederacy and Republic from courting Bothan aid to their respective side, though this only increased their stance of supporting neither faction in the Clone Wars.<ref name="The Clone Wars Campaign Guide">''[[The Clone Wars Campaign Guide]]''</ref>

Although Bothawui remained neutral during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the Bothans maintained a small defense force to protect the planet, along with Bothan colonies and economic interests. Aside from a figurehead [[Governor/Legends|governor]] and a small [[Garrison/Legends|garrison]] of [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]], there was little [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] presence. Both Imperial and [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] intelligence, by a mutual, unspoken agreement, decided to let the planet serve as neutral ground, where they could engage in their clandestine activities without risking open conflict. Bothan soldiers and officers were trained at the oft-mocked [[Bothan Martial Academy]].

[[File:AmbushThem-AoD.jpg|thumb|right|250px|A Bothan's armor is hit during an ambush]]
During the search for the new [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]], two dozen Bothans sacrificed their lives in order to attain the technical specifications for the space station. Furthermore, they learnt that the Emperor himself intended to inspect the [[Death Star II/Legends|Death Star II]], which paved the way for a Rebel attack at the unfinished weapon around [[Endor/Legends|Endor]].<ref name="TEGAS" />

Despite official neutrality, the Bothan Spynet played a significant role in military operations throughout the war. Bothan spies acquired top secret codes for the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|first Death Star]] and delivered them to rogue Imperial [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] [[Kalast]], who in turn handed them over to the Rebellion. Hundreds of Bothans would be personally slaughtered by [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] for their treachery, most notably during the [[501st Legion/Legends|501st Legion's]] retaliatory attack on the Rebel base on the surface of [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]], killing 3 Bothan Rebel leaders. Later, under the leadership of [[Koth Melan]], spies provided information to the Rebel Alliance, and were crucial in securing the [[Death Star II plans|plans]] to the second Death Star.[[File:BorskFeylya-AgentsOfDeception.jpg|left|thumb|[[Borsk Fey'lya]] was a Bothan who became chief of state.]]After the Empire subjugated the Bothan worlds, Alliance General [[Bob Hudsol/Legends|Bob Hudsol]] organized many Bothans into a resistance movement that eventually overthrew the Imperial garrison. As Bothan involvement in the New Republic increased, so did Bothan military advancement. From [[4 ABY/Legends|4.5 ABY]] to [[8 ABY/Legends|8 ABY]], the [[New Republic Defense Fleet/Legends|New Republic Defense Fleet]] maintained a Bothan-only [[Bothan Combat Response Element]] as a quick response force, giving early experience to many future Bothan officers of the New Republic. By [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]], Bothans such as [[Traest Kre'fey]] held high ranking posts in the New Republic military, and Bothan engineers had developed several warships, such as the [[Bothan Assault Cruiser]].

When the [[Second Galactic Civil War]] began in [[40 ABY/Legends|40 ABY]], the Bothan government joined the [[Corellian/Legends|Corellians]]. The Bothans began to build small, fast but durable frigates to aid the war effort and transport. [[Mon Calamari/Legends|Mon Calamari]] [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] and Chief of Staff [[Cha Niathal]] stated that the Bothans had theorized a new fleet tactic: smaller, faster ships instead of heavily armed but inherently slow [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyers]].

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:BothanConcept.jpg|thumb|left|180px|A male Bothan concept.]]
Though the famous mention of Bothans in the film [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Return of the Jedi'']] by [[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma]] did not expound on the nature of Bothans, their role and sacrifice in securing intel regarding Death Star II is well-known as a consequence.

Bothan physical appearances differ noticeably in various [[Star Wars Legends|Expanded Universe]] sources. [[Timothy Zahn]] first describes the species in his ''[[Heir to the Empire]]'' novel, and illustrations for the ''[[Heir to the Empire Sourcebook]]'' from [[West End Games]] show them as fairly Human-like creatures with fur. The ''Heir to the Empire'' comic depicts the Bothans differently, as largely fur-faced with long snouts. The [[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (comic series)|''Shadows of the Empire'' comics]] follow the lead of the West End Games sourcebooks, as do the ''[[Shadows of the Empire Planets Guide]]'', [[Star Wars: Rebellion (video game)|''Star Wars: Rebellion'']], the ''[[Star Wars Customizable Card Game]]'', and the [[Databank (original)|Databank]] (this last source uses the image from the card and was the main image for some time). Meanwhile, long-snouted Bothans appear in later EU games and publications. ''[[The Essential Guide to Planets and Moons]]'' shows Bothans as an average between the two extremes.

Though the Bothans first officially appeared in ''Heir to the Empire'', in 1991 there was a background character who incidentally looks like a Bothan in the 1985 ''[[Escape Into Terror]]'' episode of the [[Star Wars: Droids: The Adventures of R2-D2 and C-3PO|''Star Wars: Droids'']] animated television series.
